subject: Request: temporary SLA deviation for beta model deployment
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-team <platform@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary SLA deviation for beta model deployment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking our call this morning. As discussed, Acme HealthTech is planning a tightly scoped pilot of Redwood's new clinical-reasoning beta model (beta-v2) for a small set of production traffic in December. Before we spin up the pilot we need a formal exception to the standard SLA language (specifically uptime and latency commitments) for the beta period so our procurement and compliance teams can sign off.

Key asks from our side:
- Temporary uptime commitment of 99.0% during the pilot (instead of the standard 99.9%) for the first 30–60 days.
- Latency guardrails relaxed to up to p95 250ms for request/response times during the same window.
- Explicit rollback and escalation process if errors or unacceptable regressions occur.

We attached the Acme SLA request form (see attachment) with the pilot scope and volume estimates. Platform team is copied on the thread for details. We can provide a signed form once Redwood confirms the proposed deviation and any proposed mitigations (monitoring, credits, data handling).

Attachments: acme_sla_request_form.pdf (application/pdf)

Would appreciate a confirm by EOD Monday if possible so procurement can prepare the PO.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme HealthTech
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA deviation for beta model deployment

Jane — thanks for the clear write-up and the form. We're excited to move the pilot forward.

Quick responses / next steps:
- Redwood is open to a time-limited SLA deviation for beta-v2 but we need to lock down guardrails.
- Proposed pilot window: 30 days (we prefer a shorter first window to limit exposure). If Acme needs 60 days we can discuss extension contingent on monitored behavior and a joint review.
- I'll kick off an internal review with product and legal (cc'd Irene and Markus).
- Please expect a proposed exception matrix from us by EOD Monday; I'll include a DocuSign-ready SLA amendment and a monitoring checklist.

I attached an initial internal draft we can use as the starting point. Can you confirm the pilot start target date? You mentioned early December on the call.

Attachments: redwood_proposed_exception_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Acme beta SLA exception — proposed guardrails

Markus / Marissa — pulling together suggested guardrails before we send an amendment to Acme (I included Jane for transparency). High-level thoughts:

1) Window and scope
- Approve a 30-day pilot window for beta-v2 (start date requested: 2026-12-01). If Acme requests an extension to 60 days, we require a joint review at day 25 with acceptance criteria.

2) Uptime and latency deviations
- Uptime during pilot: 99.0% SLA (monthly measurement), with GA SLA (99.9%) reinstated after the pilot if metrics meet acceptance criteria.
- Latency: relax p95 target to 220–250ms (we should pick the tighter value if legal wants a clear number).

3) Monitoring, telemetry, and rollbacks
- Redwood to provide a shared monitoring dashboard (read-only link) and weekly health snapshots; automatic alerting for error-rate >1% sustained for 15 minutes.
- Immediate rollback to GA model variant if error-rate >3% sustained for 10 minutes or if a P1 is declared by Acme.

4) Financial remediation and caps
- Credits for missed uptime during pilot only; cap credits at 10% of the pilot monthly invoice.

5) Data & compliance
- Pilot endpoints limited to non-production test subset agreed in the attachment; log retention and access limited to the pilot scope.

6) Signoff workflow
- DocuSign amendment to be sent; require signature from Acme procurement + Redwood legal before pilot start.

Marissa: can you confirm acceptance of the 30-day window with Jane; Markus, can you review and advise on any legal language changes (especially the credit cap and rollback triggers)? I can draft the amendment once we agree the parameters.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme beta SLA exception — proposed guardrails

Irene / Marissa — reviewed. High-level sign-off with two edits we should propose to Acme:

1) Tighten latency number to a single, auditable figure: p95 <= 220ms for the pilot. The 250ms upper bound is too loose for contract language.

2) Clarify credit mechanics and caps: credits only apply to uptime shortfall measured monthly during the pilot period, with a cap equal to 10% of the pilot invoice (we should include an example calculation in the amendment). No ongoing credits after pilot completion.

Additionally: require a telemetry access SLA — read-only dashboard + daily aggregated CSV export for Acme during the pilot (for their compliance team). We should require Acme to notify Redwood 48 hours before any production cutover that would materially increase traffic beyond the agreed pilot volume.

If Acme agrees to the 30-day pilot, p95 <= 220ms, credit cap 10%, and the telemetry terms, I approve sending DocuSign for signature. Otherwise we can suggest a slightly longer review cadence but I would not support an open-ended 60-day exception without stronger guardrails.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA deviation for beta model deployment

Thanks everyone — Acme is good with the 30-day pilot and the updated guardrails. Confirmed acceptance:
- Pilot window: 2026-12-01 through 2026-12-30
- Uptime: 99.0% for pilot month
- Latency: p95 <= 220ms
- Credit cap: 10% of pilot invoice (understand mechanics will be shown in amendment)
- Telemetry: read-only dashboard + daily aggregated export — please share link and SSO access.

We attached a signed copy of Acme's SLA request form and the monitoring playbook for the pilot endpoints. Please send the DocuSign amendment and we'll countersign. If you can confirm the DocuSign link and monitoring dashboard by EOD we'll finalize procurement and have the PO processed.

Attachments: monitoring_playbook.pdf (application/pdf)

Best,
Jane
